governanceNotes: Deliberate deferral, not an authored suggestion: the catalog identity 'Contralateral (opposite) knee condition' is a relational claim-position concept (the knee opposite a service-connected knee), not a clinical phenotype, so its outgoing edges would need a concrete contralateral diagnosis to target - and the strongest quantified literature inverts the direction: in contralateral-ACL-injury risk cohorts the index condition is the reconstructed knee and the outcome 'contralateral condition' IS the anterior cruciate ligament injury, so an edge from this identity to the catalog acl-injury identity would restate the identity's own content rather than assert a downstream relationship.

No defensible target identity exists on the catalog: the contralateral-degeneration literature (increased radiographic and clinical osteoarthritis after ACL reconstruction or meniscectomy) is treatment-class and confounded by the original injury and meniscal status, and the common downstream outcomes (contralateral quadriceps weakness, functional asymmetry) lack catalog identities; authoring an edge to osteoarthritis or acl-injury from a relational concept would force a causal claim the source design cannot support.
